content:
The fastest land animal is the cheetah. Some key facts about the cheetah's speed:

- Top Speed: Cheetahs can reach speeds of up to 75-93 mph (120-150 km/h) in short bursts during a chase. This makes them the fastest land animal.

- Acceleration: Cheetahs can go from 0 to 60 mph (96 km/h) in just 3 seconds, which is faster than most sports cars.

- Stride Length: At their top speed, cheetahs can cover 7-8 meters (23-26 feet) in a single stride.

- Short Bursts: Cheetahs can only maintain their top speed for about 200-300 meters (0.12-0.19 miles) before they need to rest due to their bodies overheating.

Other very fast land animals include:

- Springbok antelope - Up to 55 mph (88 km/h)
- Wildebeest - Up to 50 mph (80 km/h) 
- Jackrabbit - Up to 45 mph (72 km/h)

So in summary, the cheetah is considered the undisputed champion of the fastest land animal, able to reach incredible top speeds for short bursts that no other land animal can match.
